clue.text: Provided it's accommodated in budget

definitions.meaning: given or supplied, as in 'the trip provided a break'
something one can pay for without overspending; the past tense of 'can pay for'

explanation.surface: A finance officer confirming that an expense was approved because it fits within the agreed budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford is both to supply something and to have the money for it; the past participle covers both senses.

clue.text: Scene of fighting that's on river forming country's border

parts.note: the front is where opposing armies meet in battle
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A war report about a battle fought along a river that marks the boundary between two nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' looks like a pronoun joining the phrases, but it supplies IE (that is).
explanation.definitionFit: A national boundary line, especially a contested or remote one, is called this; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wrong place for treatment before spring, going overseas

parts.note: out can mean mistaken, as in 'your figures are out'
a hospital ward is where patients are treated
to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: A patient sent to the wrong hospital ward before springtime, then heading abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is leaving port for foreign parts is described with this phrase; a nautical expression for departing abroad.

clue.text: Naturally, it enables us to see clear space

definitions.text: Naturally, it enables us to see
definitions.meaning: the light of the sun, the natural illumination by which we see
a visible gap between two things, as in 'there is now clear water between them'

explanation.surface: A cryptic musing that nature provides us with the means of sight and an open view.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunlight is the natural source of vision, and the word also means a visible gap or margin between competitors.

clue.text: Was going North on railway to create mischief

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the word for 'was' runs backwards

parts.note: to have lived is to have existed, to have been

explanation.surface: Someone travelling north by rail in order to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going North' reverses LIVED to DEVIL, a direction that only works in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish behaviour is mischief or wicked fun; a dictionary synonym.

clue.text: End of Socrates, including time in disgrace

indicators.note: the Greek letter name takes in the time abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: written in Greek, the philosopher's name ends in the letter sigma

explanation.surface: Socrates' death sentence, served out in time, as a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End of Socrates' tempts you to take a final S, but it is the whole Greek letter sigma, the last letter of his name in Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark of shame or social discredit attached to someone; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Aid distributed around El Salvador among artists

indicators.note: the rearranged letters wrap round the letter named El
aid that is distributed is spread around, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: el is the spelt-out name of the letter L

explanation.surface: Relief supplies being handed out across El Salvador, the Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'El Salvador' reads as the country, but splits: El is the letter L, Salvador starts the definition. 'distributed' turns AID into DAI, which goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador is the first name of the Spanish surrealist painter, so 'Salvador among artists' identifies him.

clue.text: Narrow lead on river, resulting in tie, perhaps

parts.note: winning by a neck is a racing term for a very small lead
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: A rowing race where a slim advantage on the river ends in a dead heat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like a drawn race, but it is the thing worn at the throat. The Wear is a river in County Durham, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A necktie is one example of clothing worn around the throat, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Judge one maiden in East, say

indicators.note: the letters for one and maiden sit inside the verb meaning say

parts.note: to state is to say or declare
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Assessing an unmarried woman in the East, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is a verb meaning STATE, into which IM goes after E. M for a maiden over in cricket: an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge a quantity roughly is to reckon or gauge it approximately; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Complaint each French person may have?

definitions.meaning: a medical complaint is an ailment, here a painful inflammation of the joints
the French saying chacun à son goût, 'each to his own taste', gives every French person a taste

explanation.surface: Asking whether every person in France might suffer from an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is French: goût means taste, and the proverb says each person has his own.
explanation.definitionFit: Joint inflammation from excess uric acid is an ailment, which in British usage is called a complaint.

clue.text: Support staff needed to make constitutional progress?

definitions.text: Support staff needed to make constitutional progress?

parts.words: Support staff needed to make constitutional progress?
parts.note: a constitutional is a health-giving walk; the staff that supports the walker is a cane

explanation.surface: A political-sounding remark that reform needs a team of back-office helpers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support staff' and 'constitutional' sound like politics and personnel; a staff is a stick, and a constitutional is a stroll taken for health.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane or staff used for support while going on foot fits a stick carried on a constitutional stroll.

clue.text: Trip organizers giving composer lots of time in camp accommodation

indicators.note: the composer and the shortened time go inside the camping word

parts.note: tents are what campers sleep in
Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Boléro

indicators.note: lots of a word is most of it, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Holiday firms rewarding a musician with a long stay in a campsite's tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lots of' means most of AGE, leaving AG; RAVEL and AG then sit after the first T of TENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Businesses that arrange journeys and holidays for customers organise trips, a plain description of the job.

clue.text: What's needed to drill child I love? Just the reverse

indicators.note: the words before supply pieces that must be read backwards to give the answer

parts.note: a girl is a female child
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about what's needed to train a child, with a twist about devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drill' suggests discipline for a child, but means boring for oil. 'Just the reverse' turns GIRL, I and O backwards to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore platform with machinery for boring wells beneath the seabed is the equipment needed for drilling.

clue.text: A book left, penned by novelist, it is okay as literature

indicators.note: something penned by a writer is enclosed inside his name

parts.note: Charles Reade was a Victorian novelist, author of The Cloister and the Hearth

explanation.surface: A critic reviewing a book a novelist abandoned and deciding it is acceptable writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Reade, a Victorian English novelist, holds A, B and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing that is pleasant and easy enough to read passes muster as literature; a fair functional description.

clue.text: Ruth seizing plunder, showing honesty

indicators.note: one word grabs another and holds it inside itself

parts.note: ruth is an old word for pity or compassion, as in ruthless
to rob is to plunder

explanation.surface: A woman named Ruth grabbing loot, which hardly displays integrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name, but is the archaic noun for compassion, surviving in 'ruthless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Probity is uprightness and integrity, a formal synonym for honesty.

clue.text: Some writing English in fifties, never meeting

parts.note: a para (paragraph) is a section of writing

indicators.note: the English abbreviation goes between the two fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty; several fifties give a run of Ls

explanation.surface: A piece of English writing by people in their fifties who never get together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fifties' looks like an age or decade but is two Roman fifties, LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lines that run side by side at a constant distance never meet; a description of the geometry.

clue.text: Unusually, a brew in here?

indicators.note: done unusually, the letters are put in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether this place, oddly, serves beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges A BREW IN. As a whole the clue jokes that a brew (beer) would be unusual in a place selling mostly wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar specialising in wine would only unusually serve a brewed drink like beer.

clue.text: Mussorgsky's introduction using trumpet a lot?

parts.note: introducing oneself begins 'I'm', so I'M is how an introduction starts
the Russian composer's first name was Modest

explanation.surface: A trumpeter playing the opening of a piece by the Russian composer Mussorgsky.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussorgsky introducing himself would say 'I'm Modest', his first name. 'trumpet' means blowing your own trumpet, boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who blows their own trumpet a great deal is boastful, the opposite of humble.

clue.text: Person who settles scores for others

definitions.text: Person who settles scores for others

parts.words: Person who settles scores for others
parts.note: settling scores sounds like revenge, but scores are musical; one who adapts music for other performers

explanation.surface: A hired avenger who takes revenge on behalf of clients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles scores' suggests revenge; musical scores are what this person prepares for others to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A musician who adapts a composition for particular voices or instruments works on scores for other performers.

clue.text: State of castaway's companion, having docked ——— look inside

indicators.note: the short word for look is placed within the shortened name
to dock a tail is to cut off its end, so the companion's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's companion in Defoe's novel about a castaway
lo is an old exclamation meaning look!

explanation.surface: Describing the condition of Crusoe's servant once the ship has berthed and someone peers inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' reads as condition but is a US state. 'having docked' trims FRIDAY to FRIDA, and LO goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-eastern peninsula is one of the fifty United States.

clue.text: Targeted person at centre of genuine counter-argument

indicators.note: one word sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: real means genuine
a butt is the target of jokes or ridicule

explanation.surface: A person singled out for attack lies at the heart of a sincere counter-argument.
explanation.definitionFit: A refutation or contradicting response offered against a claim is a counter-argument; a direct synonym.

clue.text: Head of tiny fish seen in seaweed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: A small fish's head spotted among weeds in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun but is the verb, to angle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a kind of kelp, a large brown seaweed, mainly in British and dictionary use.

clue.text: Inadequate male, a bore

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a wave surging up a river estuary

explanation.surface: Dismissing a man as a tedious, not good enough person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' suggests a dull person, but means a tidal wave up a river, also called an eagre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scanty or insufficient in amount is inadequate; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: It has long enabled movements of our capital between banks

definitions.text: It has long enabled movements of our capital between banks

parts.words: It has long enabled movements of our capital between banks
parts.note: sounds like money transfers between financial banks, but describes people crossing between the Thames riverbanks in the British capital

explanation.surface: A financial institution that has long handled transfers of the nation's money between banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' and 'banks' look financial; they are London and the banks of the Thames. This is the river crossing in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic crossing of the Thames in the City has carried Londoners from one riverbank to the other for centuries.

clue.text: Conclusions of stern judge got defendant cleared of all charges

indicators.note: the conclusion of each word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A severe judge ends a trial by acquitting the accused completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared of all charges' sounds like acquittal, but means a sum after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: A price or amount after all deductions, such as tax and fees, are taken off is net; this is a British spelling variant.

clue.text: All but one man on board st avoiding extremes

indicators.note: leaving off the extremes means dropping the first and last letters

parts.note: a knight is one of the chessmen on a chessboard

explanation.surface: Everyone except a single person aboard ship stays moderate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man on board' suggests a ship's crew; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning almost or nearly, as in 'well-nigh impossible', which is what 'all but' means.

clue.text: Championship secured in final stage with style

indicators.note: the championship word is held securely within the word for final stage

parts.note: the end is the final stage
a sporting title is a championship

explanation.surface: A sports star clinching the trophy at the last stage of the competition, and doing it elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with style' sounds like elegance, but means having a style or name, a title.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or person that has a name or title is said to be styled or named; 'style' here is a formal title.

clue.text: Creative skill is put into short article and essay

indicators.note: the word 'is' is placed inside the other pieces joined together

parts.note: art. is the short form of article
an essay is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: A student's creativity appears in a brief piece of writing and an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a school composition but means an attempt, a TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Artistic ability or craftsmanship is creative skill; a direct synonym.
